title: GD&T Fundamentals: Tolerance Zones, Datums & Dialects
subtitle: How tolerance zones turn 3D point deviations into full-width or diametral zone usage, why the driving point decides conformance, and why ASME vs. ISO must stay explicit.

standards.topic: Tolerance zones, Rule #1 envelope default, datum reference frames
Geometrical tolerancing zone shapes and feature specification

sections.heading: Zones are full widths or diameters, never half-widths
paragraphs: Every geometric tolerance defines an ideal 2D or 3D region—two parallel planes, a cylinder, a circle, a sphere, or a uniform offset surface—that must simultaneously contain all points of the toleranced feature. In `fid-gps` (`GDT.ZONE.ZTYPE`), zone usage is always reported as the full width or diameter `2 * max(d_i)` in SI metres, paired with the exact index of the driving point that attains the maximum.
This convention prevents a frequent shop-floor mistake: a hole axis shifted 0.04 mm radially from true position uses 0.08 mm of diametral position tolerance, not 0.04 mm.

sections.heading: Explicit Dialect Mapping Table (ASME vs. ISO)
paragraphs: ASME Y14.5-2018 and ISO GPS share symbols on drawings yet differ on defaults—most famously the envelope principle (ASME Rule #1) versus the independency principle (ISO 8015:2011), plus concentricity/symmetry definitions and datum-simulator association. Metrology Maven never guesses a drawing's dialect: every characteristic resolves through a versioned Dialect Mapping Table (DMT) that records exact operator chains and digests.
Under Decision D-045, every rule authored without independent credentialed sign-off stays visibly marked `interpretation: provisional` in API payloads, reports and this guide.

lab.instructions: Select a tolerance zone preset (cylindrical position zone, parallel-plane flatness/orientation zone, or unequally disposed profile offset zone), drag points on the canvas or slide the tolerance callout, and inspect the exact driving point and utilization computed live by fid-gps.

presets.label: Cylindrical Position Zone (Ø 0.10 mm)
presets.description: Three axis sample points evaluated against a Ø 0.10 mm cylindrical tolerance zone along Z. Point #2 at (-0.04, 0.03) has radial distance 0.05 mm -> exactly Ø 0.10 mm usage (100% utilized).

presets.label: Parallel-Plane Zone (0.08 mm)
presets.description: Five surface points evaluated against a symmetric 0.08 mm two-plane zone (normal +Z). Point #3 at z = -0.055 mm drives usage to 0.110 mm, exceeding tolerance.

presets.label: Unequally Disposed Profile Offset Zone (0.20 mm, UZ +0.05)
presets.description: Four profile deviations evaluated with mid-surface shifted +0.05 mm toward material (unequal bilateral profile zone of total width 0.20 mm).
